text: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is frequently complicated by ischemic tissue injury and chronic wounds, yet most single-cell studies prioritize expression and leave expressed sequence variation underused. This study proposes a mutation-derived gene-burden framework that transforms single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) reads into features for the analysis of wound-edge (WE) versus unwounded skin (UWE). Fourteen run-level observations from BioProject PRJNA736095, representing seven GEO biological samples, were aligned to GRCh38; expressed single-nucleotide variants and insertions/deletions were identified, filtered by depth, quality, alternative-read support, allele fraction, and cohort frequency, mapped to GENCODE exons, and aggregated as unique per-gene burdens. Principal component analysis, Linear SVC, penalized logistic regression, and random forest learning were evaluated with repeated stratified cross-validation. Cohort-frequency filtering reduced the median call count from 139,422 to 68,842 while increasing the first-two-component explained variance from 41.2% to 53.6%, PERMANOVA R-squared from 0.142 to 0.386, and the silhouette coefficient from 0.18 to 0.42. Linear SVC produced the strongest result, with balanced accuracy of 0.980, ROC-AUC of 0.996, and F1-score of 0.981. Coefficient analysis highlighted extracellular matrix and remodeling genes, including POSTN, COL1A1, THBS1, PLIN2, TAGLN3, and MMP9, whereas enrichment and cell-landscape integration linked WE burden to matrix organization, collagen formation, inflammation, angiogenesis, keratinocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and immune cells. The framework contributes a reproducible feature-engineering bridge between expressed variants, machine learning, pathways, and cellular context. Results are proof-of-concept because run-level dependence, small biological sample size, RNA-specific artifacts, and absent matched DNA prevent clinical or somatic-mutation claims.

text: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a progressive atherosclerotic disorder that reduces arterial perfusion of the lower extremities and ranges from asymptomatic disease to chronic limb-threatening ischemia. Current clinical guidelines recognize PAD as both a major cardiovascular risk factor and a limb-threatening condition requiring integrated medical, endovascular, surgical, and wound-care management [1]. Nevertheless, substantial gaps remain in early diagnosis and risk-factor control, particularly among older adults and patients with diabetes [2]. Impaired perfusion, tissue loss, infection, and endothelial dysfunction contribute to chronic nonhealing wounds [3,4]. Diabetic foot ulcers further aggravate tissue damage, increasing the healthcare and socioeconomic burden of chronic wounds worldwide [5,6].

provenance: supplied manuscript text; not independently reproduced
text: Bulk transcriptomic measurements cannot fully characterize chronic wounds because wound tissues contain heterogeneous populations of keratinocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, pericytes, smooth-muscle cells, and immune cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves this cellular complexity by enabling analyses of cell states, trajectories, biomarkers, and intercellular interactions. Previous studies of wound-edge tissues identified genome-wide hypermethylation and repression of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition pathways, with keratinocytes playing a dominant role [7]. Additional investigations linked endothelial PLCG2 deficiency to impaired VEGF signaling [8], while diabetic foot ulcer atlases demonstrated coordinated dysfunction across fibroblast, vascular, and immune compartments during impaired wound healing [9,10].

text: Machine learning provides an effective approach for reducing the high dimensionality of expressed-variant data while preserving biologically meaningful information. Current scRNA-seq guidelines emphasize rigorous quality control, transparent preprocessing, and appropriate biological replication [11]. Furthermore, normalization and dimensionality reduction substantially influence downstream analyses, making leakage-free validation essential [12,13]. Because coordinate-level variant matrices are sparse and difficult to interpret, aggregating accepted variants into gene-level burden features creates a more robust representation. These features can then be evaluated using standardization, variance filtering, principal component analysis (PCA), and complementary linear and nonlinear machine-learning models within repeated cross-validation.

text: This paper addresses that gap with an end-to-end framework for WE versus UWE analysis. Its contributions are: (1) an explicit expressed-variant acceptance rule combining read depth, call quality, alternative-read depth, variant allele fraction, and cohort-frequency exclusion; (2) a variant-to-gene aggregation model that constructs a sample-by-gene burden matrix; (3) leakage-aware model components for scaling, filtering, PCA, Linear SVC, logistic regression, and random forest comparison; (4) repeated stratified evaluation, pooled prediction metrics, and permutation significance assessment; and (5) biological integration of classifier coefficients with Gene Ontology, Reactome, and a 38-cluster scRNA-seq landscape. The study is presented as computational hypothesis generation. It does not claim confirmed somatic mutations, independent clinical validation, or a deployable PAD diagnostic model.

text: Droplet-based scRNA-seq enabled massively parallel transcript profiling through cell barcodes and unique molecular identifiers, establishing the technical basis for modern tissue atlases [14]. In wound repair, this resolution is important because cells with the same broad annotation can occupy inflammatory, migratory, proliferative, or matrix-remodeling states. Epidermal studies have shown that basal keratinocytes undergo state transitions during homeostasis and repair [15]. Fibroblast-centered work has likewise identified heterogeneous wound-associated populations and lineage plasticity [16]. Comparative analysis of fibrotic and regenerative dermis has revealed distinct myofibroblast and macrophage programs, including pathways related to proliferation, migration, and transforming growth factor signaling [17]. These findings complement cellular models of wound healing that organize repair into hemostatic, inflammatory, proliferative, and remodeling processes [18].

text: For chronic wounds relevant to PAD, hypoperfusion interacts with diabetes, infection, senescence, and repeated tissue injury. Reviews of pathological wound healing emphasize that delayed closure reflects failure to resolve inflammation and restore extracellular-matrix and vascular homeostasis [19]. The PRJNA736095/GSE176415 source study is particularly relevant because it compares chronic wound-edge tissue with unwounded skin and provides both expression and epigenetic context [7]. Its public single-cell component contains seven GEO samples, while the SRA organization exposes 14 sequencing runs. That hierarchy is methodologically important: runs provide computational observations, but the biological units remain the GEO samples.

text: Variant discovery from scRNA-seq is an emerging but technically constrained task. A patient-derived cell-line study showed that scRNA-seq calls can assist cellular-identity assessment when quality and allelic evidence are carefully controlled [20]. A more recent benchmark comparing bulk and single-cell strategies demonstrated that performance depends on modality, coverage, caller, and filtering design [21]. Earlier systematic comparisons also found substantial differences among single-cell RNA variant-detection methods [22]. These studies collectively reject the assumption that a generic DNA-seq pipeline can be transferred to spliced, expression-dependent RNA reads without adaptation.

provenance: supplied manuscript text; not independently reproduced
text: Specialized approaches address different parts of the problem. scAllele combines local assembly with variant detection and allele-specific splicing analysis [23]. SComatic was developed for de novo somatic-mutation discovery in high-throughput single-cell profiles and uses cross-cell evidence to suppress artifacts [24]. Monopogen integrates population priors to call single-nucleotide variants from single-cell sequencing data [25]. At the read-processing level, reliable RNA variant identification requires aggressive removal of mapping artifacts and known editing signals [26]. REDItools provides a dedicated route for RNA-editing detection [27], whereas RNA-oriented GATK workflows formalize split-read handling, recalibration, and joint-genotyping considerations [28]. In contrast, the present study uses a transparent bcftools-based call-and-filter branch and deliberately labels retained positions as expressed candidates rather than confirmed somatic variants.

text: Coordinate-level variants are often too sparse for sample-level learning. Rare-variant genetics addresses a related dimensionality problem by aggregating variants within functional units. The sequence kernel association test demonstrated that gene-level aggregation can improve power when individual rare effects are weak or heterogeneous [29]. Reviews of rare-variant association designs distinguish simple burden tests, variance-component tests, and combined approaches [30]. The current framework does not perform an association test; it adopts the representational insight that a gene is an interpretable aggregation unit. Each burden entry counts unique accepted expressed variants mapped to an exon of a given gene in a given run-level observation.

provenance: supplied manuscript text; not independently reproduced
text: High-dimensional genomic classification is vulnerable to feature leakage, unstable selection, and optimistic resampling. Guidance for machine learning in genomics recommends simple baselines, nested preprocessing, transparent evaluation units, and external validation [31]. Leakage can occur before model fitting when features are selected or transformed with information from the full cohort [32]. Small-sample cross-validation also has intrinsically large uncertainty, even when mean performance appears high [33]. Microarray research established that selecting genes before cross-validation biases prediction estimates [34], and later work showed that model selection can introduce a second layer of overfitting [35].

provenance: supplied manuscript text; not independently reproduced
text: In multi-sample scRNA-seq, pseudobulk or sample-level summaries often provide more reliable inferential units than treating cells as independent replicates [36]. Multinomial feature-selection methods illustrate how dimension reduction can stabilize single-cell representations [37]. The present analysis similarly learns from run-level gene-burden vectors rather than individual cells. Linear SVC, penalized logistic regression, PCA-based logistic regression, univariate KBest selection, and a 500-tree random forest are implemented through a common machine-learning toolkit [38]. Repeated stratification estimates resampling variability, while a label-permutation test assesses whether the observed balanced accuracy exceeds a chance distribution [39].

text: The proposed workflow contains four linked layers: data preprocessing, expressed-variant discovery, gene-burden feature construction, and machine-learning/biological interpretation. FASTQ reads are aligned to the GRCh38 reference, coordinate-sorted alignments are indexed, variants are called separately for each run, and RNA-oriented thresholds remove low-evidence records. A cohort-frequency step excludes positions observed in at least four run-level observations, thereby prioritizing less recurrent candidates. Retained coordinates are intersected with GENCODE exons, whose reference annotation supplies stable gene identifiers [40]. Unique variant positions are counted per gene and run to create the feature matrix. Scaling, feature reduction, classification, permutation testing, enrichment, and cluster integration then operate on this matrix.

text: The enrichment results must nevertheless be interpreted cautiously. Enrichment significance depends on the selected background universe, gene-set size, annotation density, and expression-dependent variant detectability. The analyzed sets were large, including 11,696 WE-higher genes and 8,523 UWE-higher genes. Large gene sets provide high statistical power but may reduce functional specificity. The pathway results should therefore be considered an organizational representation of the mutation-derived signals rather than proof that expressed variants functionally disrupt every enriched pathway. Future analyses should use a detection-aware background, restrict enrichment to stable features, incorporate predicted variant consequences, and compare pathway directions with pseudobulk differential-expression results.

text: Nevertheless, every analytical layer inherits the same sequencing-run structure and coverage-related biases. The results do not establish that POSTN or COL1A1 variants cause chronic wounds, that UWE-associated genes are biologically protective, or that a high expressed-variant burden diagnoses PAD. They demonstrate that the supplied gene-burden representation contains structured information aligned with WE/UWE labels and chronic-wound biology. The most defensible outcome is therefore a ranked validation agenda: first, inspect and genotype the loci contributing to POSTN, COL1A1, THBS1, MMP9, and the leading negative genes; second, repeat the complete pipeline using GEO-grouped folds; and third, test a locked feature-construction procedure in an independent PAD-related wound cohort.

text: From a machine-learning perspective, the strong performance of Linear SVC and regularized logistic regression is consistent with the high-dimensional and low-sample characteristics of the dataset. Linear models distribute decision evidence across correlated gene-burden features and avoid the unstable fragmentary partitions that can be produced by tree-based models. Comparable results from standardized and PCA-compressed logistic regression suggest that discrimination did not depend on one isolated coordinate. Nevertheless, the run-level performance estimates are likely optimistic for participant-level generalization. The 14 observations originated from only seven GEO biological samples, allowing related sequencing runs to occur in both training and testing partitions. Donor-grouped cross-validation, nested model selection, stability analysis, biological-sample-level confidence intervals, and independent-cohort validation are required before the framework can be compared with clinical PAD classifiers.

text: Biologically, the positive coefficients and enrichment results consistently emphasized extracellular matrix, collagen formation, adhesion, inflammatory signaling, angiogenesis, and tissue remodeling. POSTN, COL1A1, THBS1, MMP9, SPP1, and IGFBP7 are plausible components of a wound-edge program because they connect fibroblast activity, matrix turnover, leukocyte recruitment, and vascular responses. Their integration with the cellular landscape demonstrated expression across keratinocyte, fibroblast, endothelial, smooth-muscle, immune, and pericyte compartments. This multicompartment pattern is compatible with chronic-wound biology, in which failed closure results from interactions among several cellular systems rather than dysfunction in a single lineage. However, expressed-variant burden is not a direct functional assay. Matched DNA sequencing, RNA-editing annotations, spatial or protein-level validation, and perturbation studies are required to determine whether the prioritized genes reflect causal sequence variation, transcription-dependent detectability, or changes in cellular composition.

text: Four main limitations constrain the interpretation. First, only seven biological GEO samples were available, although 14 sequencing runs entered the gene-burden matrix. Second, scRNA-seq variant discovery is affected by uneven coverage, allelic dropout, transcript splicing, mapping bias, RNA editing, and ambient RNA. Third, cohort-frequency filtering may remove genuine recurrent disease-related variants while retaining systematic artifacts that occur below the selected threshold. Without matched normal DNA, the retained candidates cannot be classified as confirmed somatic mutations. Fourth, the broad enrichment universe and cell-cluster annotations may amplify well-characterized pathways. Future work should incorporate genotype-aware recalibration, population-frequency databases, RNA-editing annotations, functional-consequence weighting, donor-grouped validation, training-only feature construction, multimodal expression–burden fusion, independent PAD cohorts, and targeted DNA validation. These extensions would transform the current hypothesis-generating framework into a more credible precision-medicine evaluation pipeline.

text: This study presented an interpretable machine learning framework for transforming expressed variants identified from scRNA-seq data into gene-level burden features for integrative peripheral artery disease analysis. The framework combines splice-aware alignment, per-run variant discovery, explicit quality and allele-frequency filtering, cohort-frequency exclusion, exon-overlap annotation, gene-burden matrix construction, feature engineering, repeated cross-validation, and biological interpretation. In the analyzed PRJNA736095 dataset, cohort-frequency filtering reduced the median number of variant records by approximately one half and improved the descriptive separation between wound-edge and unwounded skin observations. Linear SVC achieved the strongest pooled classification performance, while regularized logistic regression provided interpretable coefficients for identifying influential mutation-derived genes.

text: The leading WE-associated features, including POSTN, COL1A1, THBS1, MMP9, SPP1, and IGFBP7, were linked to extracellular-matrix organization, collagen formation, inflammation, angiogenesis, adhesion, and tissue remodeling. Integration with the scRNA-seq cell landscape placed these signals within epithelial, stromal, vascular, smooth-muscle, and immune compartments. The principal advantage of the proposed approach is its multiscale interpretability: each modeled feature can be traced from an expressed variant to a gene, classifier coefficient, enriched pathway, and relevant cellular context.

text: However, the findings remain hypothesis-generating because 14 run-level observations represent only seven biological samples, RNA-derived variants were not confirmed using matched DNA, and standard run-level validation may overestimate participant-level generalization. Future work should employ donor-grouped and training-only feature construction, consequence-weighted burdens, RNA-editing controls, independent PAD cohorts, and targeted DNA validation. With these extensions, expressed-variant gene-burden modeling could provide a reproducible component of integrative PAD and chronic-wound precision research.
